chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who accepts a job/contract but does not work in it himself, and hands it over to another who profits from it. He said, 'No' (it is not permissible).

key_terms.يَدْفَعُهُ: He hands it over / delegates it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to hire someone else to do the work you contracted for in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases (*al-Ijarat*), this hadith establishes the principle of *ikhtisas* (specificity) in service contracts, where the personal skill or trust of the initial contractor is paramount. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules 'no' to delegation, indicating that unless the contract explicitly allows it, the specific individual who accepted the work cannot simply pass it to another for profit, preserving the integrity of the agreement.
